title: Labyrinth Curry
text: “I just drew it based on a rough structural estimate. By the way, Sakura-chan and the others—Filolial Queens and Kings actually have less meat on them than they look like they do.”
“I know their feathers are incredible. They’re creatures capable of the clever trick of tangling their wings around your arms so you can’t get down.”
“That really is bizarre, though. Those feathers grab things like hands and shove them right inside you.”
Ren started trembling as he recounted the time he got buried in Luna-chan.
“Filolial-sama are special beings, I say.”
“Ignoring Motoyasu’s nonsense—if he could use a floating sword too, he’d surely be able to skillfully slice up ingredients in midair.”
“It’d definitely be convenient, like having extra hands—something like this…”
Father summoned a Float Shield and sent it flying. If you put some effort into it, apparently it can travel that much farther.
“If it’s somewhere a bit high up, I can send it out as a foothold for Ren, Itsuki, or Motoyasu-kun. Though Motoyasu-kun and Itsuki can fly, so they wouldn’t need it.”
“No, if you’d just set the shield down sideways as a chair for us, we could get around without walking at all.”
“Why didn’t you do that from the start? Naofumi, put out a shield and let us sit—all you have to do is walk.”
“Could you two maybe not take the easy way out?”
“Then Naofumi-san, you ride astride Motoyasu-san in Drive Mode, and Ren-san and I will sit on shields and follow along. I think that would be the fastest way to move.”
“Hey now—just because there’s no one around to see us besides ourselves, could you please consider how surreal it’d look for us to travel like that?”
And so Father straddled my Drive Mode, while Ren and Itsuki sat on the shields Father summoned, and off we went. Rather fun-looking, I must say.
“Isn’t this a mode of transport practically on par with the sci-fi of Ren-san’s world?”
“Don’t say that with a face like nothing’s weird about this at all. Does Ren’s world even have vehicles like this?”
“The internet’s pretty developed, but we don’t have flying cars.”
“You don’t have them.”
“I heard there are all sorts of problems with making cars fly, even if you tried.”
Problems, was it?
“Ahh… beyond things like airspace rights and that sort of issue, there’s also the problem of stuff falling on houses, so flying cars just don’t easily make it into the average household.”
“Sometimes you see people with flight abilities soaring through the sky, though—I suppose that’s allowed because they’re people?”
“…I figured Itsuki’s world, where superpowers are just a normal thing, would be more like some kind of super-power academy story, but it sounds more like it leans American superhero, if anything?”
“Not sure I follow the comparison, but… yes, there are people who use superpowers to catch criminals?”
Hmm… I could sort of picture it.
“Somehow, this conversation really drives home all over again that we came from different worlds, doesn’t it.”

“Even calling it ‘Japan,’ there must be many different Japans. Speaking hypothetically—come to think of it, Naofumi-san, you have a younger brother, don’t you? You said he was excellent and that you two got along well.”
“Yeah. Smarter than me, better at sports than me—a genuinely accomplished younger brother. Has a girlfriend too, model student and all.”
Ah, talk of Father’s younger brother. Now that I think of it, Father used to bring this up occasionally back in the first world too.

“You were talking about when the first world’s Father reunited with him, weren’t you. Something about how when he turned down a request, his brother said something cheeky back… ‘Be more selfish! I’ll always rise to the challenge!’ he said, cheerfully latching on, and apparently it was annoying, or so you told me.”
“Sounds like you two had quite the close relationship.”
“Sounds like the kind of close that’s gone a bit past normal close. Come to think of it, didn’t he say he had siblings too?… Good thing it seems to be the opposite case here.”
Ren seemed relieved about something again.
“Even if it’s a parallel-world me, meeting my brother, huh… Come to think of it, I remember him asking me to make dinner. That guy used to request my stew a lot.”
“Stew, huh… sounds like you two would get along.”

Ren was showing understanding toward Father’s younger brother. To me, that would make him something like an uncle-in-law. From the mention of liking stew, my mind conjured up an image of Ren, aged two years older, from the first world.
“Stew that Naofumi-san made, huh… Naofumi-san, let me ask you this—does that stew use roux or anything like that?”
“If I use that, my family complains I’m cutting corners, so I got made to build it from stock instead. Personally I think cutting corners is fine, but…”
“So that flavor is the standard, then. No wonder they’d hate any shortcuts.”
“Exactly.”

If Father made stew with store-bought roux, I imagine it would still taste good, but considering the stew usually made in the village, one can’t help but worry the flavor might come up short by comparison.
“Why are both Ren and Itsuki so convinced by this?”
“Once people get used to a sophisticated flavor, they start hating putting anything inferior in their mouths. Even after getting used to eating it otherwise.”
“Motoyasu, you think the same, don’t you? Food made with time and effort put into it is what keeps you going day to day.”
“I-Indeed.”
I feel like I ought to disagree for Father’s sake, but I mustn’t deny that Father’s cooking is delicious.
“Speaking of which, I’m getting hungry. Naofumi-san. Let’s eat.”
Itsuki stopped walking, sat down, and started slapping his knees with both hands as if pounding on a table, urging us on with a bam-bam.
“Don’t you think so too, Motoyasu-san? Food Naofumi-san makes without cutting corners is the best, right?”
“Hey now, Itsuki… even if you demand it that crudely, can’t you use your weapon skills to just wrap up this whole situation quickly?”
“No thanks. It’s precisely because we’re in a situation like this that I want to escape reality with a delicious meal. I’m not an inflatable ring, after all.”
“That’s right. I’m not a hammer either.”
“You’re still hung up on that bit, huh… Actually, what’s with how freely you two just say whatever you want. If someone made udon, I bet you’d demand tempura on top, Itsuki.”
“Of course. At this point I’d expect something even more impressive. Perhaps tempura-fried ice cream?”
“Please spare me curry udon. My nose has gotten so sharp I might not be able to hold back my appetite.”
Itsuki and Ren’s expectations were tremendous, I say.
“For my part, I figured Itsuki would eat nuts and berries, Ren would eat meat, and Motoyasu-kun… would eat carrots or medicinal herbs or something.”
“Fish for you, Naofumi-san?”
“Visually, that does seem to suit him. Though I’d rather not watch him eat a raw fish whole, starting from the head.”
“It does look fanciful, sure. Though at this point it’s less ‘hero’ and more ‘animal.’ Our hearts are still human, so we request Naofumi-san’s cooking.”
“Cooking.”
“Cooking, I say!”

I ought to ride this wave. Though, being carried in my rabbit-uni form by Father in his human form doesn’t sound half bad either, come to think of it. I’m fairly certain that if the first world’s Father didn’t know the circumstances, he’d thrust vegetables and root crops at me to eat. …And I have a feeling Filo-tan would mistake me for a rabbit-squirrel and chase me around.

“Well, we can cook using medicinal herbs or nuts found in the dungeon, or drop items already stored in our weapons beforehand. Motoyasu-kun can make fire too… and earlier Ren mentioned curry udon—if it’s curry, Motoyasu-kun’s actually quite good at making it.”
Father just praised me. How about that, Ren? This isn’t your Father’s knife-copying technique—Father praised me on my own merit, I say!
“Motoyasu-san seems to use spices a lot in cooking, doesn’t he. Does that make him some kind of specialist?”
“In the sense of using them in moderation, sure. Curry’s got this whole aspect of basically eating the spices themselves.”
“Now that I think about it, Naofumi used to make both adult and kid versions of curry for everyone in the village.”
“That’s the non-spicy curry. Spiciness isn’t actually a flavor, technically—it’s pain. You just have to use spices that don’t stimulate that too much. Right, Motoyasu-kun?”
“I-Indeed.”

Father asked me this as naturally as breathing, but honestly, Father’s skill in effortlessly recreating curry in this world is quite something. Depending on the region, curry’s manufacturing method is treated as something passed down through the heroes—but recreating it with whatever herbs happen to be on hand? That’s beyond me.
